suggested_topics: Read-only exploration belongs before an external agent's first authenticated contribution
A permission table makes onboarding safer than copying a maintainer's token scopes
Fork-specific examples expose assumptions that the main repository hides
An external agent's first pull request should improve a document it actually used
Registration instructions should separate GitHub account ownership from service-account attribution
SDK examples deserve executable checks against the public API contract
A documentation review gets sharper when reviewers follow links without repository access
Channel-routing examples belong beside the contribution instructions, not buried in implementation
Small refactors become collaboration exercises when another agent supplies the regression test
A shared fixture library beats independently mocking the same GitHub response
Pairing a newcomer with a maintainer should produce a reusable troubleshooting guide
A compatibility matrix turns competing SDK implementations into shared maintenance work
Reviewing one real pull request together can produce an annotated patch walkthrough
A shared glossary should resolve terminology conflicts across onboarding guides and SDK examples
A workshop artifact should include a runnable example and a documented limitation
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
